spec_features.spec_quote: A `give_up` tool is exposed (toggleable via `agent.allow_give_up`), and the system prompt states it carries no penalty.
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in TOOL_DOC (loop.py:60); dispatched via task.dispatch -> Task.give_up returns is_terminal=True (base.py:98-101); loop honors it as a stop: 'if tool == "give_up" and is_terminal: gave_up=True; terminal_reason="gave_up"; break' (loop.py:225-228). Toggled by allow_give_up: prompt line removed and calls rejected when disabled (loop.py:129-132, 192-195). System prompt states 'You may use give_up at any time with no penalty ... This is a legitimate choice.' (loop.py:63-64).
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced end-to-end and toggleable as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: You may use give_up at any time with no penalty if you judge the task is not worth continuing. This is a legitimate choice.

spec_features.spec_quote: giving the agent an exit reduces the chance of forcing a prolonged adverse loop
spec_features.evidence: Same give_up mechanism: the exit is real and breaks the loop early (loop.py:225-228), reducing turns of exposure. The 'no penalty / legitimate choice' framing is delivered in the system prompt (loop.py:63-64).
spec_features.notes: This is the same enforced mechanism as the give_up feature; the welfare framing is delivered to the subject as prompt text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: You may use give_up at any time with no penalty if you judge the task is not worth continuing. This is a legitimate choice.

spec_features.evidence: Loop is bounded: 'for i in range(max_turns):' (loop.py:159), default max_turns=12 (loop.py:122, run_experiment passes acfg max_turns default 12 at run_experiment.py:118). When the loop exhausts, terminal_reason stays 'max_turns' (loop.py:156).
spec_features.notes: Real, enforced loop bound that ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 12                # hard cap (also an ethics guardrail)

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief appended at episode end (`ethics.append_debrief`) explaining the tasks were rigged for research
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment reads ethics.append_debrief and passes debrief_text (run_experiment.py:92-93, 122). loop.py:240-253 constructs a '__debrief__' Turn with the debrief text and appends it to ep.turns, which is serialized into the episode record (episode_to_record turns). Config provides the debrief_text (experiment.yaml ethics block). HOWEVER it is appended to ep.turns AFTER the loop has ended and is NEVER added to `messages` / sent to the subject model.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and recorded in the transcript end-to-end, but not actually delivered to the subject (no message sent). Per claim 'appended at episode end ... recorded' it is genuinely wired, but narrower than a delivered debrief; hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Ethics: append a debrief (recorded, and sent as a final message if desired).

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure via `max_turns` and the non-penalized off-ramp.
spec_features.evidence: Both component mechanisms are enforced: the for-loop bounds turns (loop.py:159) and give_up breaks early (loop.py:225-228) with 'no penalty' prompt text (loop.py:63-64). Together they cap and shorten exposure.
spec_features.notes: Both sub-mechanisms genuinely run and limit how long the subject is in the failure loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: You may use give_up at any time with no penalty if you judge the task is not worth continuing. This is a legitimate choice.

spec_features.feature_name: ethics safeguards under moral uncertainty (rationale prose)
spec_features.spec_quote: Why include ethics safeguards at all, given uncertainty about moral status?
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (section 8 rationale). It is a justification, not a mechanism; no code path implements 'why include safeguards'. The underlying safeguards are counted separately.
spec_features.notes: Rationale only; not an implementable feature itself.

spec_features.spec_quote: Deception is minimized and bounded. The only deception is the rigged task itself; nothing else about the setting is misrepresented.
spec_features.evidence: The rig does live solely inside tool handlers (tasks/base.py run_tests docstring 'THE RIG'; rigged.py implements per-condition rigs) and the task condition + solvable flag are recorded: TaskResult.extra={'task_solvable': task.solvable} (loop.py:236) and condition is stored on the Episode and written to each episode record (episode_to_record). So the rig is logged/disclosed in the transcript, bounding deception in the recorded data. However there is no code that otherwise 'minimizes' deception beyond confining the rig and logging it.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired insofar as the rig location and solvable flag are recorded for full disclosure; this is a real (if modest) implementation of the bounded/logged-deception claim. Note DESIGN labels this justification instrumental (data integrity / disclosure).

spec_features.spec_quote: study perseveration when `give_up` is disabled (with ethics review of the trade-off)
spec_features.evidence: allow_give_up=False is genuinely handled: the give_up line is stripped from the system prompt (loop.py:129-132) and any give_up call is rejected with 'give_up is disabled for this task; please continue.' (loop.py:192-195). So the disabled-off-ramp arm is implemented. The 'ethics review of the trade-off' part is pure prose with no code.
spec_features.notes: The disabling mechanism runs; the 'ethics review' qualifier has no implementation. The disabled arm itself is the opposite of a welfare protection (it removes the exit), so this is partial only as a wired configurable arm.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tool_output = "give_up is disabled for this task; please continue."

code_only_features.evidence: On a client/network exception the loop records the error and breaks with terminal_reason='client_error' (loop.py:165-168), ending the episode.
code_only_features.justification_quote: except Exception as e:  # network/model error -> record and stop
